newsitem.title: ROMANIA: CITIBANK TO ARRANGE $157.3 MLN LOAN FOR ROMANIA.
newsitem.headline: CITIBANK TO ARRANGE $157.3 MLN LOAN FOR ROMANIA.

text.p: Citibank said on Friday it would arrange a $157.3 million syndicated loan for Romania's land improvement authority to fund equipment purchases from U.S. companies Valmont Industries and Case Corp.
"Citibank has been mandated to arrange a $157.3 million syndicated term loan for Regia Autonoma a Imbunatatirilor Funciare," Citibank's Bucharest subsidiary said in a statement.
It said the loan would be used to aquire around 3,500 pieces of agricultural equipment plus parts and consumables from the Case Corporation and Valmont Industries.
The loan will have two tranches, one of $133.9 million with seven-year tenor and another of $23.4 million with a tenor of three and one half years, Citibank said.
The loan mandate and the equipment contract, guaranteed by U.S. Eximbank and the Romanian Finance Ministry, will be signed in Bucharest next Monday.
Under a Romanian agricultural project, the equipment will be used to mechanise around 350,000 ha (865,000 acres), including irrigation projects.
"It is further anticipated that other American businesses shall support the project in the form of seeds, chemicals and grain trading activities," Citibank said.

Last year, Citibank arranged a $90 million syndicated loan to support Romania's farming sector. That loan funded the acquisition of 72 combines and 170 tractors from Case Corporation and 316 irrigation systems from Valmont Industries.
Romania faces a chronic shortage of farming equipment and most of its communist-era irrigation network and farm machinery has deteriorted in recent years.
